title: Data governance for AI in Thailand and Vietnam: Navigating converging privacy and AI governance regimes
headline: Data governance for AI in Thailand and Vietnam
summary: Thailand and Vietnam are shaping responsible AI governance by intersecting personal data protection laws with emerging AI-specific regulatory regimes. In Thailand, governance relies on the Personal Data Protection Act alongside new digital platform rules and a draft AI act. In Vietnam, the legal framework is developing through a new Law on Artificial Intelligence and accompanying decrees.
why_it_matters: The overlap between data privacy rules and emerging AI obligations presents material compliance considerations for stakeholders across all stages of AI development and use.

quotes.text: In both jurisdictions, personal data protection laws currently exert substantial influence across the AI life cycle — from data collection and model training to deployment and continuing operation — by regulating the collection, processing and use of personal data within AI systems.
The resulting overlap between data privacy rules and emerging AI obligations presents material compliance considerations for stakeholders across all stages of AI development and use.

dates_mentioned.what: Draft Principles of AI Act released for public consultation by the Electronic Transactions Development Agency
dates_mentioned.quote: Draft Principles of AI Act , released by the Electronic Transactions Development Agency for public consultation 2 July 2026

dates_mentioned.what: Decree No. 142/2026/ND-CP supporting the Law on Artificial Intelligence in Vietnam

classification.significance_reason: Provides regional analysis of converging privacy and AI regulations in Thailand and Vietnam for international practitioners.
